title: Normalized integral Tate tower coefficient and projection data
statement: Use the lifted p-adic DVR and its ideal (ell), the uniquely residue-normalized finite quotient comparisons, their associated-module realizations, the projection-normalized comparison of completed coefficient rings, the actual inverse-root tensor powers and their strict quotient towers. Define ProjectionBalanced and ProjectionNormalized by the actual root projections and exact single/evaluation maps; define Reconstructed by actual inverse-limit counits and IdentifiesExceptional by the finite gamma square. All constructions and names are those previously attached to lem-pur-condensed-tate-integral-tower; no mathematical definition changes. proof.text: Auxiliary coefficient claims, now proved in Lean: identify each positive power quotient of the universe-lifted p-adic integers with ZMod using toZModPow and its kernel. Finiteness gives additive torsion. The lifted DVR is a Noetherian PID, so the existing scalar perfect-cohomology/PID-model theorem applied to the explicit rank-one quotient surjection gives perfectness. Quotient induction proves uniqueness of the residue-normalized ring equivalence. Its inverse followed by the continuous-function scalar presentation is locally bijective; the existing associated-module realization equivalence gives exactness. Residue compatibility and naturality of the scalar presentation on an explicit quotient-ring diagram give the scalar square for every comparable pair. The diagram uses the actual quotient homomorphisms, with identity and composition supplied by the existing Ideal.Quotient.factor laws; the existing consecutive scalar squares determine its natural transformation. Derived realization is an equivalence, so the existing inverse-mate theorem proves invertibility of the specified scalar mate. The finite coefficient isomorphisms commute with adjacent maps by the same residue computation. They define a natural isomorphism of inverse systems, whose induced limit isomorphism has the required projection equations; joint monicity of limit projections proves uniqueness. These arguments prove coefficientProperties, residueIso_existsUnique, scalars_locallyBijective, realization_exact, scalars_comp, scalarComparisonMap_isIso, and completionIso_existsUnique. The main condensedTateIntegralTower theorem remains open with the eight preceding proof steps retained.
